Caveat: Why is it missing?

Below, no young IQ was ever observed. No imputer fixes this. The question is not which method to use but why those rows are missing, and that answer lives in how the data was collected

Four Options for a Hole

Top to bottom, each one uses more of the rest of the record

Imputation as EstimationFilling a hole from the rest of the data

x̂ij = f( Xobserved )every filled cell is a prediction from the rest of the table
Every filled cell is an estimate, not an observation

Caveat: Mean ImputationEvery hole gets the same value, and the spread of the column collapses

Mean stays 2.08; standard deviation falls to 1.76 and a spike appears

Observed and Filled ValuesUse other observed columns to find comparable rows

The filled number is an estimate; keep its origin distinguishable

k-Nearest Neighbor (kNN) Imputation

x̂ij = (1/k) ∑r ∈ Nk(i) xrjclosest in the other columns, or in an embedding of them
Average similar rows; including all observed rows gives the column mean

Demo: Imputation MethodsOne column of cycle times, 1,200 rows: every fill changes the column

1. Compare mean and kNN fill.   2. What changes when the helper column contains little information?

Answer: Imputation ChoicesCompare distributions, not only the filled cells

ChoiceWhat to inspect
Mean fillMean can stay close; variance shrinks
kNN fillDoes the helper column contain information?
Missingness maskKeep observed and estimated cells distinguishable
A filled cell is an estimate, not a new observation

Regression Imputation

x̂ij = b0 + ∑m≠j bm ximno residual is added back, so the spread shrinks
Deterministic predictions remove residual variation and can make correlation look stronger

Noise and Outliers

Raw Sensor StreamsMetered power demand, with two different kinds of error mixed in

Blue spikes drop to zero and below. That is the meter dropping out, not demand

Noise vs OutliersSmooth measurement noise; investigate outliers before changing them

Smoothing changes values; removal drops rows

Smoothing by Binning

Twelve values become three distinct ones. Smoothing buys steadiness with resolution

Moving Averages for StreamsSimple (SMA) and exponential (EMA) moving averages use only current and past samples

x̂t = (1/w) ∑k=0w−1 xt−k·st = α xt + (1 − α) st−1SMA weights the window equally; EMA uses one α
Both use past samples; here EMA crosses four samples before SMA

Demo: Smoothing a StreamCurrent and past cycle times (seconds); wider trailing windows respond later

1. Compare windows 1, 5 and 11.   2. When does the smoothed signal cross 68 s?
5

Answer: Smoothing DelayA larger trailing window needs more new observations

WindowFirst smoothed value ≥ 68 sDelay after t = 30
1300 samples
5322 samples
11355 samples
Less fluctuation comes with a later response

Outlier Detection by Statistics

zi = (xi − x̄) / soroutside Q1 − 1.5·IQR, Q3 + 1.5·IQRthe z-score uses the mean; the fence uses only quartiles
Separate column fences can miss an unlikely combination of otherwise ordinary values

Demo: IQR Fence Width300 cycle times with eight sensor glitches and eight genuinely slow cycles

1. Change the fence width.   2. Which genuine cycles disappear along with sensor glitches?
drop anything outside Q1 − k·IQR … Q3 + k·IQR

One-Class ClassificationDraw a boundary around normal and flag what falls outside

A learned boundary checks combinations that separate column fences miss

Caveat: Irreversible CleaningCleaning cannot be undone downstream

Deleting the spike removes the evidence needed to revisit the decision

Rule-Based ChecksDomain knowledge determines which consistency rules are valid

CheckRow it stopsWhere the rule comes from
shipped ≥ orderedA-1042How the business works
qty = 0 → amount = 0A-1043How the business works
unit ∈ { kg }A-1044A decision someone has to make
Three rules flag three rows; verify the recorded values before training

Three Questions of Integration

Schema Mapping

Same Name, Different Entity

Order and Shipment are separate entities here; their names alone do not define the schema

Mapping Two Schemas into One

Matched elements collapse into one. What only one side has still has to fit somewhere

Demo: Mapping Customer RecordsMatch meaning before matching rows

Source fieldTarget fieldTransform or decision
CRM.Name / ERP.CompanyParty.nameretain name variants
CRM.customer_id / ERP.account_idsource_idkeep source + original ID
CRM.booked_amount / ERP.net_salesseparatedifferent measures
1. Do booked_amount and net_sales belong in one column?
2. Do matching column names prove matching customers?

Answer: A Shared SchemaAlign field meanings while preserving different measures and source identifiers

Target fieldSource mappingMeaning
name + aliasesCRM.Name / ERP.Companyorganization names
source / source_idCRM ID / SCM ID / ERP IDoriginal identifiers
booked_amountCRM.booked_amountbooked orders
net_salesERP.net_salesrecognized net sales
Mapping columns does not establish that two rows refer to the same entity

Mapping Fields and Preserving IDsAlign field meanings now; establish shared identity after record matching

CRM fieldERP fieldIntegrated field
Customer.NameAccount.CompanyParty.name
Customer.PhoneAccount.PhoneParty.phone
—Account.EmailParty.email
customer_idaccount_idsource + source_id
Matching column meanings does not prove that two records describe the same party

Duplicate Detection

Demo: Exact DuplicatesNormalize, then drop_duplicates: twelve supplier rows, six real suppliers

1. Normalize until six suppliers remain.   2. What breaks when you keep only the first word?

Answer: Normalization and MergingA shorter string can accidentally erase a real distinction

NormalizationResult in this example
Case, punctuation, spaces, suffixes12 rows → 6 suppliers
Keep only the first wordDistinct Samsung and POSCO entities merge
Preserve original name and source IDThe decision remains auditable
Normalization should support matching without hiding the original record

name · phone · source_id

Fuzzy MatchingEach field gets a similarity score, then one weighted total against a cutoff

score = ∑f wf · simf(a, b)·sim = 1 − edit(a,b) / max(|a|,|b|)on lowercased text, then one weighted total
Per-field scores become one number. The cutoff you pick trades false merges against missed ones

Learned MatchingLearned representations compare records beyond exact spelling

Input

Two candidate records

Model

Encode fields and estimate similarity

Decision

A score proposes a match; evidence confirms it

Learned similarity can link different spellings; identity still needs evidence

LLM-Assisted MatchingLarge language models (LLMs) propose the matches, humans verify them

Input

Candidate names and record fields

Model

Retrieve evidence and propose a match

Review

Verify identity before merging records

Models propose candidates; verified identity supports a merge

Fusion

Conflicts After MatchingMatched rows still disagree on values

Same customer, three spellings of one address, three phone numbers

Rules About the Source

Neither rule reads the value. One keeps a stale address, the other keeps a typo

Rules About the Value

x̂ = argmaxv ∑k wk · 1[xk = v]weighted vote: wk is the trust in source k
Three copies of one value count as one vote, not three

Demo: Resolving a Customer ConflictChoose a canonical value and keep the evidence

FieldCandidate valuesEvidence
nameHanil Precision / 한일정밀(주)same verified registration ID
address12 / 12, 5F / Teheranro 12verified delivery: 12, 5F
phone02-555-0100 / 02-555-0199 / 010-2233-4455no fresh confirmation
1. Which values can be settled now?
2. Which field needs a review instead of a vote?

Answer: A Canonical CustomerPublish resolved values while keeping unresolved conflicts visible

party_idfieldcanonical valueevidence / status
P-073nameHanil Precisionverified ID; aliases retained
P-073addressTeheran-ro 12, 5Fverified delivery + ERP
P-073phoneNULLreview; candidates retained
A canonical record includes provenance and unresolved decisions

Takeaway: Cleaning and Integration

DecisionWhat must remain clear
Repair a valueObserved, estimated or verified against the source
Flag an errorA contradiction identifies a problem, not its replacement
Merge recordsField meaning, entity identity and conflict resolution
Preserve original evidence and record why each value or identity changed
